title: Code Visibility Across Files
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of code visibility across files using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates code visibility across files.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Code Visibility Across Files** as part of **Packages, Modules, Dependencies, and Build Tools**. Catch or represent expected failures at a boundary where the program can respond usefully; do not silently swallow errors or expose secrets in messages. Use the subtopics—Public and Internal APIs, File-Level Declarations, Managing Package Boundaries—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Real projects depend on reliable error handling, modular organization, reproducible builds, and safe language boundaries. This lesson helps turn isolated syntax into maintainable applications.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Catch or represent expected failures at a boundary where the program can respond usefully; do not silently swallow errors or expose secrets in messages.

content_blocks.title: How to reason about it
content_blocks.text: Start with public and internal apis. Then compare it with file-level declarations. Identify the input, state, dependency, or branch that determines the result. The snippet is a static reference for CodeLeaf and is not executed in the lesson page.

items.title: Public and Internal APIs
items.text: Public and Internal APIs crosses a system boundary. Model success and failure, validate external data, apply timeout/retry rules deliberately, and keep credentials and database access out of presentation code.

items.title: File-Level Declarations
items.text: File-Level Declarations is one part of code visibility across files. Connect its definition to the example, identify the input/state it changes, and verify the expected behavior with a small test case.

items.title: Managing Package Boundaries
items.text: Managing Package Boundaries is part of reproducible project configuration. Declare the dependency or plugin where it belongs, preserve a compatible version set, and use the Gradle Wrapper for repeatable builds.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Save the snippet in a Kotlin/JVM console project and run the configured Gradle application task, or use the Kotlin Playground for examples that need no external dependencies.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the documented starting values, rerun the smallest test, and compare the result with the expected output. If behavior differs, check the compiler/plugin/runtime versions and the active target before changing more than one thing.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: Code Visibility Across Files removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset
content_blocks.text: If the example fails, first confirm which runtime/project type the snippet requires. Read the first useful compiler or runtime message, check imports and declared dependencies, reduce the example to a minimal case, and rerun. For target-specific code, use the target toolchain rather than assuming a console or browser runner can execute it.
